plan.scenario: When a user reports accidentally booking two same-day flights and wants to cancel one, and multiple reservations share a date.
plan.experience: Before asking the user which reservation to cancel, evaluate cancellation eligibility for ALL candidate same-day reservations (booked within 24h, airline cancelled, business cabin, or insurance covering the reason) and present the user with the eligible option(s) first, so the user is not led to pick an ineligible booking and the task can actually be completed.

plan.scenario: When a user requests cancellation of a reservation and claims prior approval from customer support, but the reservation does not meet standard cancellation eligibility criteria.
plan.experience: Collect the user ID, reservation ID, and cancellation reason, then verify all eligibility conditions (booked within 24h, airline-cancelled, business cabin, or insurance covering the stated reason). If ineligible, deny with a clear explanation and never override policy or grant exceptions. Transfer to a human agent only if the user insists on prior approval or escalation.

plan.scenario: When a user requests cancellation of a reservation that does not meet standard eligibility criteria (not within 24h, not airline-cancelled, not business cabin, no insurance covering the reason).
plan.experience: Verify eligibility against all policy conditions and, if ineligible, deny the cancellation with a clear explanation; transfer to a human agent if the user insists on escalation or requests compensation, an exception, or a refund beyond policy.

plan.scenario: When a user requests a date change on a reservation that is in basic economy and therefore non-modifiable.
plan.experience: Plan to verify the cabin class and policy eligibility first; if basic economy, deny the modification with a clear explanation, mention any insurance-based cancellation alternative, and offer transfer to a human agent if the user insists or requests escalation.

plan.scenario: When a user requests a cabin upgrade for all passengers plus adding checked bags under their membership, with a possible budget constraint.
plan.experience: Plan to first retrieve reservation and user details, verify cabin-change eligibility (no basic economy, no flown segment, uniform cabin across all passengers/segments), compute the full price difference for all passengers, check membership-based baggage allowance per cabin, and require explicit confirmation before any update. Anticipate that partial (single-passenger) cabin changes are not allowed and be ready to offer the baggage-only alternative.

plan.scenario: When a user asks for information that is outside the agent's scope (e.g., the cause of a flight delay) and also requests compensation or escalation.
plan.experience: Plan to state clearly that the requested information cannot be provided and avoid speculation; offer only in-scope help (booking, modification, cancellation, refunds/compensation). If the user insists on the out-of-scope information or requests escalation, plan to transfer to a human agent with a summary noting no booking action was taken.

plan.scenario: When a user requests flight changes (date/route) plus later cabin/baggage changes on an existing reservation.
plan.experience: First retrieve the reservation and verify modifiability, then check policy gates (no origin/destination/trip-type change, cabin-change restrictions, baggage add-only, insurance not waiving voluntary-change fare differences) and inform the user which flexible options are actually searchable. Determine the target date from the original reservation, search both direct and one-stop flights, compare eligible cabin fares (treating cabin upgrades as applying to the whole reservation), and compute fare differences/refunds. Require explicit confirmation before each database update.

plan.scenario: When booking a flight reservation with user constraints (time windows, cabin, payment preferences) and policy gates (passenger limits, payment method limits, baggage allowances).
plan.experience: Plan a strict sequence: obtain user id and profile first, search flights, filter by all user constraints (e.g., departure time, cabin), collect passenger details, insurance, and baggage, then verify policy gates (one certificate max, passenger limit, membership baggage allowance) and require explicit confirmation of the full summary before calling the booking API.

plan.scenario: When a user requests cancellation and refund citing illness and claims travel insurance was purchased, but the reservation may not actually include insurance.
plan.experience: Plan to verify insurance status directly from the reservation record and payment history before relying on the user's claim; check all eligibility criteria (24h window, airline cancellation, cabin class, insurance coverage) and deny with clear reasons if none apply, offering human transfer only if the user insists or disputes the record.

plan.scenario: When a user requests compensation for a flight delay but explicitly refuses to change or cancel the reservation.
plan.experience: Verify the reservation and flight-status facts first, then clearly state that delay-only compensation is not available under policy and that any certificate/refund requires a change or cancellation, without speculating on delay causes or historical records. If the user declines both and insists on an exception or escalation, firmly deny and transfer to a human with a summary noting no booking action was taken.

plan.scenario: When a user asks to remove a passenger from an existing reservation.
plan.experience: Plan to first retrieve the reservation and confirm the passenger list, then check the policy gate that passenger count cannot be changed; if removal would alter the count, deny removal and proactively offer valid alternatives (e.g., replacing the passenger while keeping the count, or transferring to a human agent).

plan.scenario: When a user requests a cabin upgrade on an existing reservation that is in basic economy (or otherwise non-modifiable), and also asks about payment balances.
plan.experience: Plan to first check modification gates (basic economy blocks any change including cabin), then if blocked, evaluate cancellation eligibility and propose cancel-and-rebook as the path; also plan to compare single-reservation vs split-reservation payment allocation when per-reservation limits on certificates/gift cards would otherwise push more onto a credit card.

plan.scenario: When a user requests changing a passenger's name on an existing reservation.
plan.experience: Plan to retrieve the reservation first, confirm the passenger list and which passenger is being renamed, collect the new first/last name and DOB, verify the passenger count remains unchanged and flights/cabin stay the same, then present the proposed edit and require explicit user confirmation before calling the update tool.

exec.scenario: When executing a cancellation request where the reservation is ineligible and the user claims a prior approval from customer support.
exec.experience: After confirming ineligibility, clearly state the denial and reasons. If the user requests escalation or an exception, mentions a prior approval, or asks for a voucher/gift card, offer a human transfer via transfer_to_human_agents with a summary noting no cancellation action was taken; if they decline the transfer but keep demanding an exception, firmly confirm you cannot override policy. Never attempt to cancel or override policy.

exec.scenario: When booking a reservation with a user-specified payment method order (e.g., certificates first, then gift cards, then a specific credit card for the remainder).
exec.experience: Verify the exact payment method IDs from the user profile before booking; use the specific card the user named (e.g., the MasterCard) for the remainder rather than any available credit card, and double-check the payment_methods list in the book_reservation call matches the user's stated order and card.

exec.scenario: When executing a denied modification request for a non-modifiable (basic economy) reservation and the user asks for an exception or escalation.
exec.experience: After confirming ineligibility, clearly state the denial and reasons, offer any applicable alternative (e.g., insurance-covered cancellation), and if the user insists or requests a human, use the transfer_to_human_agents tool with a summary noting no modification was made.

exec.scenario: When executing a baggage addition after a cabin upgrade is declined and the user confirms baggage-only changes.
exec.experience: Call update_reservation_baggages with the total bag count and nonfree_baggages computed from the membership allowance for the current cabin (free bags => nonfree_baggages=0), and only after explicit user confirmation; then confirm the result to the user.

exec.scenario: When a user requests cancellation of multiple reservations, some eligible and some not, and also asks for escalation of the ineligible one plus additional account information.
exec.experience: Handle independent sub-requests in parallel: gather the requested account info, escalate the ineligible reservation via transfer_to_human_agents, but still complete the eligible cancellation (after explicit confirmation) rather than letting the transfer end the episode with the eligible cancellation unexecuted. Confirm and call the cancel API for the eligible reservation before or alongside the transfer.

exec.scenario: When executing flight changes and ancillary updates on a reservation with a budget constraint and a user claiming insurance waives fees.
exec.experience: Search direct flights for the requested dates, filter by the user's time window, compute per-segment fare differences and net refund/charge, clarify that insurance covers cancellation refunds not voluntary-change fees, deny options exceeding the user's budget or violating whole-reservation cabin rules, and apply updates with the correct payment method after explicit confirmation.

exec.scenario: When executing a multi-part change request (flight dates, cabin, baggage) with a user-imposed budget cap and a user claim that insurance waives change fees.
exec.experience: Search and filter flights per the user's constraints, compute the exact package total and fare difference, explicitly state that insurance covers cancellation refunds but not voluntary-change fare differences, and if the user conditions the change on a fee waiver or budget cap that cannot be met, cancel the entire request without partial changes or unauthorized updates.

exec.scenario: When executing a booking where the user specifies a payment preference order and constraints on flights.
exec.experience: Filter search results against the user's stated constraints before presenting options; when the user requests multiple certificates but policy allows only one, apply the larger certificate and put the remainder on the user-specified card; confirm the exact payment split and total before booking.

exec.scenario: When executing a cancellation request where the user insists insurance was purchased but the reservation record shows no insurance.
exec.experience: Re-fetch the reservation details to confirm, cite concrete evidence (insurance flag and payment history showing no insurance fee), clearly explain ineligibility, and transfer to a human agent only when the user explicitly requests escalation; do not cancel or override policy.

exec.scenario: When executing a delay-compensation request where the user refuses change/cancel and asks for escalation or case opening.
exec.experience: Check status for all relevant segments, clearly report that only current status is visible (not historical delays), state the compensation-requires-change/cancel policy, and when the user insists on escalation, call transfer_to_human_agents with a summary capturing reservation facts, membership, insurance, and that no booking action was taken.

exec.scenario: When executing a cabin downgrade for all passengers on a reservation with a refund to the original payment method.
exec.experience: Search current fares for the same flights, compute the new total and refund against the original amount, present the breakdown and any fare-rule consequences (non-refundable/non-modifiable), obtain explicit confirmation, then call update_reservation_flights with the same flight numbers/dates, the new cabin, and the original payment_id.

exec.scenario: When executing a cancel-and-rebook with multiple passengers and a user-specified payment priority (certificates, then gift cards, then a specific credit card), possibly split into separate reservations to maximize certificate usage.
exec.experience: Verify cancellation eligibility (within 24h, no flown segments) before cancelling; search both direct and one-stop flights for each direction and compute cheapest business combinations; when per-reservation payment limits apply, compute MasterCard charge under single vs split plans and present both; then execute cancellation first, followed by each booking with the exact payment method IDs and amounts the user approved.

exec.scenario: When executing a passenger name change on a reservation.
exec.experience: Retrieve reservation details to confirm the current passenger list, present the exact before/after passenger details for confirmation, and only after explicit user confirmation call update_reservation_passengers with the full updated passenger list (preserving unchanged passengers and DOB).

exec.scenario: When executing a flight change that includes a cabin change and a possible refund, with the user open to alternate destinations.
exec.experience: Search both direct and one-stop options for the permitted route and date, filter to the requested cabin (excluding Basic Economy), present the cheapest eligible itineraries with per-segment fares and total, compute the refund/charge versus the original amount, confirm the refund payment method exists in the profile, and only call the update API after explicit user confirmation.
